title: [ML] Report thread settings per node for trained model deployments

timeline.message:
[ML] Report thread settings per node for trained model deployments

When a trained model deployment is started the user may request specific
number of threads for inference and/or parallel forwarding. However,
when the pytorch process starts these settings are adjusted so that
the actual number of threads doesn't exceed the available number of
threads. This commit changes the result format so that other type of
results may be read from the process than just inference results.
We then introduce a result for reading the thread settings from the
process and we report it in the response of the trained model _stats API.
timeline.author: Dimitris Athanasiou

timeline.body: Add a `continue` statement here. If there is an inference results there will not be a thread setting

reply.body: It doesn't hurt to not have it like this though. I know we'll probably not be compounding results together, but we follow this pattern for autodetect and analytics. I'd rather we kept it like this here too.

timeline.body:
`LongSummaryStatistics` is not thread safe which is why this method was previously synchronized. 

Perhaps extract the line `timingStats.accept(inferenceResult.getTimeMs());` into a separate synchronized method

reply.body: Ah, well spotted. I added those two lines in a `synchronized` block.
